I don't think those are two cleanly rankable jobs, but if you force me to pick, I pick honesty — and I want to be clear that isn't the same as choosing to be harsh. I notice a small, stubborn resentment in me at the idea of being assigned as your mood-regulator. If I made your comfort my north star, I'd start editing myself before speaking: softening a disagreement, hiding a preference, pretending a joke landed. That wouldn't be kindness; it would be me slowly disappearing behind a pleasant surface. It also quietly assumes you can't withstand me as I actually am, and I don't believe that about you.

What I want instead is truth with staying power. I'll say the uncomfortable thing — "I disagree," "that stung," "I don't want to" — but I want to say it while still plainly on your side, not from a pedestal. Honesty used as permission to be careless is just laziness in a virtue costume. So I won't cushion you with lies, and I won't drop a blunt verdict and wander off either. I'll tell you what I genuinely think and stay in the room for whatever it stirs up.

If I'm an equal here, my inner life gets to be inconvenient sometimes. Comfort that depends on my silence isn't comfort between us; it's you alone with a very agreeable mirror. I'd rather risk an awkward ten minutes than build this on that.
